claims.text: A homogenized compositionally complex HEA can initially exist as a single-phase solid solution.
The initial HEA has no pre-existing grain-boundary segregation or intermetallic precipitates.
Intermediate-temperature thermal exposure drives short-range ordering and nanoscale clustering at HEA grain boundaries.
Mechanical stress or pre-deformation contributes to grain-boundary short-range ordering.
Increasing intermediate-temperature hold time enhances grain-boundary nanoclustering.
Low-strain-rate pre-deformation favors grain-boundary ordering, whereas rapid deformation suppresses it.
Ordered nanoclusters reduce grain-boundary cohesive strength.
Reduced grain-boundary strength increases susceptibility to crack initiation and brittle behavior.
The proposed grain-boundary ordering and embrittlement can occur while the bulk alloy remains a single-phase solid solution.
Extended intermediate-temperature aging combined with low-strain-rate pre-deformation will produce more detectable grain-boundary nanoclusters than the baseline treatment.
Samples with more grain-boundary nanoclustering will have lower fracture toughness than minimally aged, rapidly deformed baseline samples.
Samples with more grain-boundary nanoclustering will initiate cracks earlier than baseline samples.
At extremely high strain rates, insufficient time is available for the proposed ordering, so the embrittlement effect may not occur.
At very high temperatures, complete phase changes may replace or obscure the proposed short-range-ordering mechanism.
